name: Adaptex-RM
description: Adaptex-RM is a magneto-rheological composite textile developed by Tessera Materials in collaboration with Veilweave Textiles, consisting of iron-rich particle chains suspended in a polymer matrix that transitions from supple fabric-like flexibility to near-rigid plate hardness within 40 milliseconds when an embedded micro-coil network generates a directed magnetic field. The material can be tuned to any stiffness point along its range — not just two states — allowing gradual or dynamic stiffness profiling across different zones of a garment or panel simultaneously. Powered by inductive charging, the system holds a charge sufficient for 6 hours of active stiffness cycling.
applications: Adaptive body armor that softens for movement and hardens on impact
Medical exoskeleton liners for joint stabilization
Smart industrial gloves for precision-to-power-grip transitions
cost: Φ 780 per sq meter (controller unit: Φ 290)
story_hooks: A runner's Adaptex-RM suit has been remotely compromised — someone can lock it rigid at will, turning their protection into a prison mid-operation.

A Tier 2 knockoff version of Adaptex-RM has hit the street market with a dangerous flaw: the stiffness transition is uncontrolled, snapping rigid without warning and breaking the bones of the people it's supposed to protect.

A street medic has jury-rigged salvaged Adaptex-RM panels into improvised traction splints for a trauma clinic in the Shelf — but Tessera's IP enforcement drones are scanning for unlicensed activation signatures.
